findings.fix: Add a case to cmd/tests/test_routine_worktree.sh that makes routine_chain_sync_main land HEAD on a stray branch (or stubs it to do so) and asserts routine_worktree_create removes the worktree/branch and returns non-zero.
findings.claim: routine_worktree_create (routines/_lib/worktree.sh:169-172) gained a new failure branch — discard the fresh worktree/branch when, after a successful routine_chain_sync_main, HEAD is not on the newly created dated branch $new (guarding against merge-resolve leaving HEAD on a stray merge/* work branch) — but no test in this diff exercises that path: cmd/tests/test_routine_worktree.sh exists but is unchanged in this diff (not among this chunk's files, confirmed via `find cmd/tests -iname '*worktree*'` and the manifest's empty partners list), and no other test file in this chunk's 'files' list references routine_worktree_create's symbolic-ref check.
findings.evidence: Re-read routines/_lib/worktree.sh lines 161-176 (git show 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e): the diff adds `|| [[ "$(git -C "$wt" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null)" != "$new" ]]` to the discard condition, with a comment explaining the stray merge/* branch risk. Re-checked cmd/tests/ directory listing — test_routine_worktree.sh is present but git diff --numstat against the base commit shows no change to it, and it is absent from this lane's manifest 'files' array, so it was not touched to cover the new branch. This is new conditional logic per ACTION-REVIEW-TEST-001 ('Unit or integration tests added for core logic') with no accompanying test in the reviewed diff; exposure is rare because it only triggers when chain sync succeeds (no conflict, or a resolved conflict) yet HEAD ends up off the dated branch — effect is debt (an unverified safety guard), not a user-facing break.
